label: dig
intro: Query any domain's DNS records — A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME, SOA or PTR — straight from a real dig binary running in your browser.
description: dig is the standard tool for inspecting DNS records. Point it at a domain to see how it resolves, which mail servers handle it, or which name servers are authoritative for it. You can target a specific resolver with @server, +short trims the output to just the answer, and +dnssec asks the resolver to include DNSSEC signature (RRSIG) records and the ad (authenticated data) flag.
useCases: Check that a new A/AAAA record has propagated after a DNS change
Find the MX records to confirm where a domain's email is routed
Look up TXT records (SPF, DKIM, domain verification) for troubleshooting
Check with +dnssec whether a domain's DNSSEC signatures validate

label: whois
intro: Look up who registered a domain, when it was created, when it expires, and which registrar and name servers manage it.
description: whois queries the domain registry's public record for a given domain. It's the fastest way to check registration and expiry dates, registrar details, and delegated name servers without installing anything locally.
useCases: Check when a domain you're interested in was registered or will expire
Identify the registrar and name servers behind a domain
Basic due diligence before buying or trusting a domain

label: host
intro: A lighter, more concise alternative to dig for a quick DNS resolution check.
description: host resolves a domain name to its IP addresses (and vice versa) with compact, human-readable output — useful when you just want a fast yes/no on whether a name resolves, optionally against a specific DNS server.
useCases: Quickly confirm a hostname resolves at all
Sanity-check DNS from a specific resolver while debugging propagation

label: curl
intro: Send a real HTTP(S) request — GET, POST or HEAD, with custom headers — and see the response headers or body live in your browser.
helpSyntax: curl [-I|-i|-L] [-X GET|POST|HEAD|PUT|DELETE] [-H "key: value"]... [-A ua|--user-agent ua] [-d data] url
description: curl is the standard tool for probing web servers and APIs. Use -I for headers only, -L to follow redirects, -H to add request headers, -A (or --user-agent) to set the User-Agent, and -d to send a request body. Only http:// and https:// URLs are allowed, and requests run with a forced timeout and output-size limit.
useCases: Check response headers, status code and redirects for a URL
Verify a REST API endpoint responds as expected
Confirm security headers (HSTS, CSP, etc.) are present on a site

label: openssl s_client
h2: openssl s_client — online TLS certificate checker
intro: Open a TLS connection to any host:port and inspect the certificate chain it presents.
description: openssl s_client establishes a real TLS handshake against a server and prints the certificate it receives — issuer, validity dates, and (with -showcerts) the full chain. -servername sets SNI, which most modern hosts require to return the right certificate.
useCases: Check a certificate's expiry date before it causes an outage
Confirm SNI is configured correctly for a multi-domain server
Inspect the full certificate chain for a TLS misconfiguration

label: mtr
h2: mtr — online traceroute / network path tool
intro: See the network path to a host and the latency/loss at each hop, combining traceroute and ping into one report.
description: mtr traces the route packets take to a host and repeatedly probes each hop, so you can see exactly where latency or packet loss is happening along the path. Runs here in report mode (-r) with a capped packet count.
useCases: Diagnose which network hop is causing latency or packet loss
Compare a network path over IPv4 vs IPv6

label: ping
intro: Send a handful of ICMP echo requests to a host and see round-trip time and packet loss.
description: ping is the simplest way to check whether a host is reachable and how long a round trip takes. Runs here with a capped packet count, so it's a quick reachability check rather than a continuous stream.
useCases: Confirm a host is up and reachable from the public internet
Get a rough sense of latency to a server before deeper debugging

label: nc
h2: nc — online TCP port connectivity check
intro: Check whether a single TCP port on a host is open and accepting connections.
description: nc (netcat) here runs strictly as a one-shot connect check (-zv) against a single host:port — it reports whether the port is open, closed, or filtered. Listen mode and arbitrary data exchange are intentionally not available.
useCases: Verify a specific port (e.g. a database or app port) is reachable from outside
Quickly confirm a firewall rule change took effect
